### `discussion_board_content_reports`

Member-submitted reports flagging articles for policy violations or
inappropriate content.

Stores community-driven content moderation reports where members flag
articles that may violate community guidelines, contain spam,
misinformation, offensive content, or other policy violations. Each
report captures the reporting member's concerns, selected violation
category, and optional detailed explanation.

Reports are added to the moderation queue for moderator review. Multiple
members can report the same article independently, with each report
tracked separately. Moderators review reports and take appropriate action
(approve content, edit content, or remove content), then mark reports as
resolved.

The reporting system enables collaborative content quality management by
empowering the community to identify problematic content while
maintaining moderator oversight and final decision authority.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Reported article that allegedly violates community guidelines. {@link
  > discussion_board_articles.id}.
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Member who submitted this content report. {@link
  > discussion_board_members.id}.
- `resolved_by_moderator_id`
  > Moderator who reviewed and resolved this report. Null if report is still
  > pending review. [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators).
- `report_category`
  > Category of policy violation being reported. Valid values include 'Spam',
  > 'Offensive Content', 'Misinformation', 'Off-Topic', 'Other'. Helps
  > moderators prioritize and categorize reports.
- `report_details`
  > Optional detailed explanation from the reporter describing the specific
  > policy violation or concern. Provides context to help moderators
  > understand the issue.
- `status`
  > Current resolution status of the report. Valid values: 'pending'
  > (awaiting moderator review), 'reviewed_no_action' (moderator found no
  > violation), 'reviewed_edited' (moderator edited content),
  > 'reviewed_removed' (moderator removed content). Tracks report lifecycle.
- `resolution_notes`
  > Moderator's notes explaining the resolution decision. Provides
  > transparency about why the report was handled in a specific way. Null if
  > report is still pending.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the report was submitted by the member. Used for
  > prioritizing older reports and tracking moderation response time.
- `resolved_at`
  > Timestamp when the report was reviewed and resolved by a moderator. Null
  > if report is still pending. Used for measuring moderation response time.

### `discussion_board_moderation_logs`

Comprehensive audit trail of all moderator actions for accountability and
transparency.

Records every content moderation and user management action taken by
moderators, including article edits, article deletions, attachment
removals, account suspensions, and account bans. Each log entry captures
what action was taken, which moderator performed it, what content or user
was affected, when it occurred, and the moderator's documented reason.

The moderation log serves multiple critical purposes: accountability
(tracking who did what and why), transparency (allowing review of
moderation decisions), dispute resolution (providing evidence for
appeals), and pattern analysis (identifying problematic content or users
requiring escalated action).

Log entries are immutable and retained indefinitely per business
requirements. Moderators and administrators can search and filter logs by
action type, moderator, affected content, affected user, or time period
to review moderation history, investigate specific incidents, or generate
moderation activity reports.

This comprehensive audit trail ensures moderation decisions are
documented, reviewable, and consistent with community guidelines.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_moderator_id`
  > Moderator who performed this moderation action. {@link
  > discussion_board_moderators.id}.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Article that was moderated (edited, deleted, or had attachments removed).
  > Null if action was user account management rather than content
  > moderation. [discussion_board_articles.id](#discussion_board_articles).
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Member whose account was affected by moderator action (suspension, ban,
  > or account restoration). Null if action was content moderation rather
  > than account management. [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members).
- `action_type`
  > Type of moderation action performed. Valid values: 'article_edited'
  > (moderator edited article content), 'article_deleted' (moderator removed
  > article), 'attachment_removed' (moderator deleted specific attachment),
  > 'account_suspended' (member account temporarily suspended),
  > 'account_banned' (member account permanently banned), 'account_restored'
  > (suspension or ban reversed). Categorizes the moderation action.
- `reason`
  > Moderator's documented explanation for taking this action. Required for
  > all moderation actions to ensure accountability and transparency.
  > Examples: 'Removed spam content', 'Suspended for harassment', 'Edited to
  > remove personal information'.
- `action_details`
  > Additional contextual details about the moderation action. May include
  > what was changed in an edit, which attachment was removed, or specific
  > policy violations. Provides complete context for audit trail.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the moderation action was performed. Used for
  > chronological audit trail, moderation activity reporting, and tracking
  > response times.

### `discussion_board_account_actions`

Record of account-level moderation actions including suspensions and bans.

Tracks all temporary suspensions and permanent bans applied to member
accounts, maintaining a complete history of disciplinary actions. Each
record captures which member was affected, which moderator applied the
action, the reason for the action, the duration (for suspensions), and
the current status (active, expired, or reversed).

Temporary suspensions prevent members from logging in and creating
content for a specified duration (1, 7, 14, or 30 days). When the
suspension period expires, the account is automatically restored to
active status. Permanent bans prevent all future access and are typically
reserved for severe or repeated policy violations.

Moderators can reverse suspensions or bans if they were applied in error.
All status changes are tracked with timestamps to maintain a complete
audit trail. The action history helps moderators make informed decisions
about escalating enforcement (warnings → short suspension → long
suspension → permanent ban) based on violation patterns.

This table enables moderators to search and filter account actions by
affected member, moderating moderator, action type, or time period to
review enforcement history and ensure consistent application of community
guidelines.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_member_id`
  > Member whose account was suspended or banned. {@link
  > discussion_board_members.id}.
- `discussion_board_moderator_id`
  > Moderator who applied this account suspension or ban. {@link
  > discussion_board_moderators.id}.
- `reversed_by_moderator_id`
  > Moderator who reversed or lifted this suspension or ban. Null if action
  > has not been reversed. [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators).
- `action_type`
  > Type of account action applied. Valid values: 'suspension' (temporary
  > account block), 'ban' (permanent account block). Determines whether the
  > action has an expiration date.
- `reason`
  > Moderator's documented reason for suspending or banning the account.
  > Required for accountability and to inform the affected member. Examples:
  > 'Repeated spam violations', 'Harassment of other members', 'Severe policy
  > violation'.
- `duration_days`
  > Duration of suspension in days (1, 7, 14, or 30 days). Null for permanent
  > bans which have no expiration. Used to calculate expiration timestamp for
  > temporary suspensions.
- `status`
  > Current status of the account action. Valid values: 'active' (currently
  > in effect), 'expired' (suspension period ended), 'reversed' (moderator
  > lifted the action). Determines whether the member is currently blocked.
- `reversal_reason`
  > Explanation for why the suspension or ban was reversed by a moderator.
  > Null if action has not been reversed. Examples: 'Applied in error', 'User
  > successfully appealed', 'Circumstances changed'.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the suspension or ban was applied. Used to calculate
  > expiration time for temporary suspensions and to track enforcement
  > history chronologically.
- `expires_at`
  > Timestamp when a temporary suspension will automatically expire and the
  > account will be restored. Null for permanent bans. System automatically
  > updates status to 'expired' when this time is reached.
- `reversed_at`
  > Timestamp when a moderator reversed or lifted the suspension or ban. Null
  > if action has not been reversed. Tracks when account access was manually
  > restored.

operations.specification: Guest registration (join) operation for the discussion_board_guests table. This endpoint creates a new guest session for anonymous visitors who want to browse the discussion board. The operation generates a unique session identifier and tracks basic analytics data including IP address, user agent, and visit timestamps. This is a public endpoint that requires no authentication and serves as the entry point for anonymous users to access read-only content on the platform.
operations.description:
Creates a new guest session for unauthenticated visitors to browse the discussion board with read-only access to public content.

This operation registers a new guest user by generating a unique session identifier and capturing essential browsing analytics. The session identifier is stored in the browser to track the guest's activity across visits, enabling analytics on traffic patterns and potential conversion to registered membership. The endpoint collects IP address and user agent information for security monitoring and device analytics while maintaining privacy through anonymous session tracking.

The operation writes to the discussion_board_guests table, creating a record with session_identifier (unique browser-stored token), ip_address (for security monitoring), user_agent (for device analytics), first_visit_at and last_visit_at timestamps (both set to current time), and page_views initialized to zero. All fields are non-nullable as defined in the Prisma schema.

Guests receive JWT tokens upon registration that grant read-only access to published articles, article lists, and public discussions. They cannot create content, comment, upload attachments, or access moderation features. When guests later register as members, this guest record can be linked to track the conversion journey from anonymous browsing to active participation.

Security considerations include rate limiting on guest session creation to prevent abuse, IP-based tracking for security monitoring per the schema's ip_address field, and automatic session expiration based on the last_visit_at timestamp. The unique session_identifier index ensures each guest session is distinct and prevents duplicate session creation.

This is a public endpoint with authorizationActor set to null, as it must be accessible to unauthenticated visitors. The response returns JWT tokens (access and refresh) along with the guest session details, following the IDiscussionBoardGuest.IAuthorized response type pattern for authentication operations.
operations.summary: Register new guest session for anonymous browsing access to discussion board content

requestBody.description: Guest session creation data including session identifier, IP address, and user agent

responseBody.description: Guest session details with JWT access and refresh tokens

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Token refresh operation for guest users of the discussion_board_guests table. This endpoint allows guests to obtain new JWT access tokens using a valid refresh token, extending their browsing session without requiring re-registration. The operation updates the last_visit_at timestamp to track ongoing engagement and maintains continuity of the guest's read-only access to public content.
operations.description:
Refreshes JWT access tokens for guest users to maintain continuous browsing sessions and read-only access to discussion board content.

This operation enables guests to renew their authentication tokens using a valid refresh token, extending their session lifetime without interrupting their browsing experience. The relationship to the specific member is maintained through discussion_board_password_reset_of_members, which creates a linking record with the discussion_board_password_reset_id and discussion_board_member_id foreign keys. This subtype table enables proper 3NF normalization while supporting password resets for both members and moderators through the same base table.

The generated token is sent to the member's registered email address with instructions to complete the password reset process. The token is valid for 1 hour for security purposes. Members can request multiple password reset emails, with each request creating a new token; however, only unused tokens (used_at is null) can be successfully redeemed.

This operation is public and requires no authentication, as it's specifically designed for users who cannot log in due to forgotten passwords. It's the first step in the password recovery workflow, followed by the password change operation (POST /auth/member/password/reset/complete) which consumes the token and updates the member's password in discussion_board_members.

The password is never stored or transmitted in plain text, maintaining security standards consistent with the initial registration process. The reset token is marked as consumed by setting used_at to the current timestamp in discussion_board_password_resets, preventing token reuse.

As a security measure, all existing sessions in discussion_board_member_sessions for this member are invalidated by setting their expired_at timestamp, forcing re-authentication with the new password across all devices. It returns complete verification details including the associated member, email address, token expiration status, and verification completion timestamp. This operation is used by moderators to inspect individual verification records and by the system to process verification token validation.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information about a specific email verification record
operations.description:
Retrieve complete details of a specific email verification record by its unique identifier.

This operation fetches comprehensive information about a single email verification record including the verification token metadata, associated member account, target email address, creation timestamp, expiration timestamp, and verification completion status. The operation is essential for moderators reviewing verification workflows and for system processes validating verification tokens.

The verification record contains critical security information for the email verification workflow. When a member registers, a verification record is created with a unique token sent to their email address. The token is valid for 24 hours (as specified in expires_at field). Members must click the verification link containing the token to complete email verification and activate their account.

Security considerations: This operation requires moderator authentication to prevent unauthorized access to verification tokens and sensitive member email addresses. The operation returns the complete verification record including token value, which should only be accessible to authorized moderators for troubleshooting purposes. Member-facing verification processes use different endpoints that validate tokens without exposing full record details.

The response includes all fields from the discussion_board_email_verifications table including the member relationship details. The verified_at field indicates whether verification was completed (non-null) or is still pending (null). The expires_at field allows moderators to determine if a token has expired and whether a new verification email should be sent.

This operation references the discussion_board_email_verifications Prisma schema and includes the related discussion_board_members information through the foreign key relationship. Error handling includes validation for non-existent verification IDs and proper permission checks for moderator access.

parameters.name: verificationId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target email verification record

responseBody.description: Complete email verification record with member details and verification status

operations.summary: Create email verification token for member registration
operations.description:
Create a new email verification record and send verification email to a member's registered email address. This operation generates a unique verification token valid for 24 hours and sends it to the member's email.

Email verification is required before members can create articles and access full platform features. Upon registration, a verification token is automatically generated through this endpoint and sent to the member's email address. Members can also request new verification emails if the original token expires.

The operation validates that the member account exists and is not already verified. It generates a cryptographically secure random token, stores it in the discussion_board_email_verifications table with a 24-hour expiration timestamp, and triggers the email sending process. Each verification record contains the token, target email address, and expiration details.

Security considerations include rate limiting to prevent abuse (maximum 3 verification emails per member per hour) and token uniqueness validation. The verification token is single-use and invalidated after successful verification or expiration.

Related operations: Members complete verification by accessing the verification link sent via email, which triggers a separate verification confirmation process.

requestBody.description: Member email verification request details

responseBody.description: Created email verification record with token details

operations.specification: This operation initiates a password reset request for members or moderators who have forgotten their password. It operates on the discussion_board_password_resets table along with the actor-specific subtype tables (discussion_board_password_reset_of_members or discussion_board_password_reset_of_moderators) to generate secure password reset tokens.
operations.summary: Request password reset token for account recovery
operations.description:
Initiate a password reset request by generating a secure reset token and sending it to the user's registered email address. This operation supports both member and moderator accounts through polymorphic actor pattern.

The operation validates that the provided email address exists in either the discussion_board_members or discussion_board_moderators table. It generates a cryptographically secure random token, stores it in the discussion_board_password_resets table with a 1-hour expiration timestamp, and creates the corresponding subtype record (discussion_board_password_reset_of_members or discussion_board_password_reset_of_moderators) to maintain proper normalization.

Password reset tokens are sent to the user's registered email address and allow users to set a new password without knowing their current password. Each reset request includes the actor_type discriminator field to distinguish between member and moderator requests. The token is single-use and invalidated after successful password change.

Security measures include rate limiting (maximum 3 password reset requests per email per hour) to prevent abuse, and the system does not reveal whether an email address exists in the database to prevent account enumeration attacks. Previous reset tokens for the same account are invalidated when a new request is made.

The operation uses PATCH method because it requires complex request data (email address and actor type) to search for the appropriate account and initiate the reset process. After successful token generation, users receive an email with a reset link valid for 1 hour.

Related operations: Users complete password reset by accessing the reset link sent via email, which triggers a separate password change operation that validates the token and updates the password.

requestBody.description: Password reset request with email and actor type

responseBody.description: Password reset confirmation with token expiration details

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information about a specific password reset request by its unique identifier. It operates on the discussion_board_password_resets table and returns comprehensive reset request data including the target email address, expiration timestamp, usage status, and associated actor information (member or moderator). The operation determines the actor type through the polymorphic relationship maintained via discussion_board_password_reset_of_members and discussion_board_password_reset_of_moderators junction tables. SECURITY NOTE: The password reset token field is intentionally excluded from the response as it is a sensitive security credential that must not be exposed.
operations.summary: Retrieve a specific password reset request by ID (token excluded for security)
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a password reset request identified by its unique ID from the discussion_board_password_resets table.

This operation returns comprehensive password reset request data including the target email address, expiration timestamp (1 hour validity), usage status, and creation timestamp. The response identifies whether the reset request was initiated by a member or moderator through the actor_type discriminator field.

The system uses a polymorphic ownership pattern where password resets can be associated with either members or moderators. The actual relationship to the specific member or moderator account is maintained through separate junction tables (discussion_board_password_reset_of_members and discussion_board_password_reset_of_moderators), following the Compatible Actor Pattern for proper database normalization.

Security considerations: This endpoint is restricted to moderator access only. The password reset token field is intentionally excluded from the response as it is a sensitive security credential. Exposing the token would allow unauthorized password changes. Tokens are single-use, expire after 1 hour, and are invalidated immediately upon successful password change. The used_at timestamp indicates whether a token has been consumed.

Use cases include administrative review of password reset requests, debugging reset flow issues, and monitoring reset token usage patterns for security auditing. The used_at timestamp helps identify pending versus completed reset requests.

parameters.name: resetId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the password reset request

responseBody.description: Password reset request details (token excluded for security)

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of account-level moderation actions including suspensions and bans from the discussion_board_account_actions table. It supports complex search criteria including filtering by affected member, moderating moderator, action type (suspension/ban), status (active/expired/reversed), and time period. The operation enables moderators to review enforcement history, track disciplinary patterns, and ensure consistent application of community guidelines.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated list of account moderation actions
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of account-level moderation actions from the discussion_board_account_actions table.

This operation provides comprehensive querying capabilities for reviewing the complete history of member account suspensions and bans. Moderators can filter by multiple criteria including the affected member (to view a specific member's disciplinary history), the moderating moderator (to review actions taken by a specific moderator), action type (temporary suspension or permanent ban), current status (active, expired, or reversed), and time period (actions within a specific date range).

Each account action record captures complete context including which member was suspended or banned, which moderator applied the action, the documented reason for the action, the duration (for temporary suspensions), and the current enforcement status. The operation returns paginated results sorted by creation timestamp to show most recent enforcement actions first.

Suspensions are temporary account blocks that prevent members from logging in and creating content for a specified period (1, 7, 14, or 30 days). When the suspension expires, the account is automatically restored to active status. Permanent bans prevent all future access and are reserved for severe or repeated policy violations. Moderators can reverse suspensions and bans if they were applied in error, with all reversals logged for accountability.

This search operation is essential for several moderation workflows: reviewing a specific member's enforcement history before applying escalated discipline, auditing moderator actions to ensure consistent guideline enforcement, generating moderation activity reports for administrative oversight, and identifying patterns of repeat violations that may require permanent bans.

The response includes complete action details, associated member and moderator information, timestamps for all status transitions (created, expired, reversed), and the full audit trail of reasons and reversal justifications. This comprehensive view enables informed moderation decisions based on complete enforcement context.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering account actions

responseBody.description: Paginated list of account moderation actions matching search criteria

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information about a specific account action (suspension or ban) by its unique identifier. It operates on the discussion_board_account_actions table and returns comprehensive details including the action type, affected member, moderating moderator, reason, duration, status, and all relevant timestamps. This endpoint is essential for moderators to review enforcement history and verify the details of past disciplinary actions.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information about a specific account suspension or ban action
operations.description:
Retrieve complete details about a specific account-level moderation action including suspensions and bans applied to member accounts.

This operation accesses the discussion_board_account_actions table to return comprehensive information about a single disciplinary action. The response includes the action type (suspension or ban), the affected member's identity, which moderator applied the action, the documented reason, duration (for temporary suspensions), current status (active, expired, or reversed), and all associated timestamps.

Moderators use this endpoint to review enforcement history when making decisions about escalating violations or handling appeals. The detailed action record shows whether a suspension has expired, if it was reversed by another moderator, and the complete rationale documented at the time of enforcement. This supports consistent application of community guidelines and provides transparency in moderation decisions.

The operation validates that the actionId parameter corresponds to an existing account action record. Access is restricted to moderators only, as account action details contain sensitive information about member discipline. The response includes foreign key relationships to both the affected member and the moderating moderator, enabling complete context for enforcement actions.

This endpoint does not modify any data—it is a read-only operation for reviewing enforcement history. Related operations include searching account actions (PATCH /accountActions) and creating new account actions (POST /accountActions).

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the account action to retrieve

responseBody.description: Detailed account action information including action type, affected member, moderator, reason, duration, status, and timestamps

operations.specification: This operation creates a new account-level moderation action, applying either a temporary suspension or permanent ban to a member account. It operates on the discussion_board_account_actions table and is invoked when moderators enforce disciplinary measures for policy violations. The operation requires the moderator to specify the affected member, action type (suspension or ban), documented reason, and duration (for suspensions). Upon successful creation, it records the complete enforcement action with timestamps and returns the created action record.
operations.summary: Create a new account suspension or ban action against a member account
operations.description:
Apply a temporary suspension or permanent ban to a member account for policy violations, creating a complete enforcement record in the discussion_board_account_actions table.

This operation enables moderators to take disciplinary action against member accounts that violate community guidelines. When invoked, the system creates a new account action record capturing the action type (suspension or ban), the affected member, the moderating moderator (extracted from JWT authentication), the documented reason for enforcement, and the duration for temporary suspensions.

For temporary suspensions, the moderator specifies a duration (1, 7, 14, or 30 days), and the system calculates the expiration timestamp. The member's account status is immediately updated to prevent login and content creation during the suspension period. When the suspension expires, the system automatically restores account access. For permanent bans, no expiration is set, and the member is permanently blocked from all future access.

The operation enforces business rules requiring a documented reason for all enforcement actions to maintain accountability and transparency. The moderator's identity is automatically captured from the authenticated session, creating a complete audit trail. The status is initially set to 'active' for new actions.

This endpoint supports the progressive enforcement model defined in the moderation requirements, where repeated violations lead to escalating consequences (warnings → short suspension → long suspension → permanent ban). Moderators reference the member's violation history before applying enforcement to ensure proportional and consistent discipline.

Upon successful creation, the operation returns the complete account action record including all calculated fields and timestamps. The affected member receives an email notification explaining the action, duration, and reason. Related operations include viewing account actions (GET /accountActions/{actionId}) and searching enforcement history (PATCH /accountActions).

requestBody.description: Account action details including affected member, action type, reason, and duration for creating new suspension or ban

responseBody.description: Created account action record with all enforcement details and timestamps

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing account action (suspension or ban) in the discussion_board_account_actions table. It allows moderators to modify the details of a previously applied account suspension or ban, such as changing the duration, updating the reason, or reversing the action. The operation operates on a specific account action identified by the actionId path parameter.
operations.summary: Update an existing account action (suspension or ban) on a member account
operations.description:
Update the details of an existing account action that was previously applied to a member account. This operation allows moderators to modify suspension or ban records, including changing the duration of temporary suspensions, updating the documented reason for the action, or reversing the action entirely.

The discussion_board_account_actions table tracks all temporary suspensions and permanent bans applied to member accounts. Each action record contains the action type (suspension or ban), the reason for the action, the duration (for suspensions), and the current status (active, expired, or reversed). Moderators can update these fields to correct errors, adjust enforcement based on new information, or reverse actions that were applied incorrectly.

When reversing an action, the moderator must provide a reversal reason explaining why the original action is being lifted. The system records which moderator reversed the action and when it was reversed, maintaining a complete audit trail for accountability and transparency. Reversing a suspension or ban immediately restores the member's account access.

Security and authorization: Only authenticated moderators can update account actions. The moderator performing the update is recorded in the audit trail. The operation validates that the action_type remains consistent (cannot change suspension to ban or vice versa without creating a new action). Status transitions must follow valid state flows (active → reversed, active → expired for suspensions).

Business rules enforced: Duration updates for suspensions must use valid values (1, 7, 14, or 30 days). Reversal operations require both reversal_reason and reversed_by_moderator_id to be set. The expires_at timestamp is recalculated when duration_days is modified. All modifications are logged in the discussion_board_moderation_logs table for comprehensive oversight.

Related operations: This operation works in conjunction with account action creation (POST /accountActions) and retrieval (GET /accountActions/{actionId}). Moderators typically review account actions before updating them, and may need to query the member's complete enforcement history to make informed decisions about modifications.

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the account action to update

requestBody.description: Updated account action details including reason, duration, status, and reversal information

responseBody.description: Updated account action record with all current details

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes an account action record from the discussion_board_account_actions table. It removes the historical record of a suspension or ban that was applied to a member account. The operation operates on a specific account action identified by the actionId path parameter.
operations.summary: Permanently remove an account action record from the system
operations.description:
Permanently remove a specific account action record from the system. This operation deletes the historical record of a suspension or ban that was previously applied to a member account. The deletion is permanent and cannot be reversed, removing the action from the member's enforcement history and moderation logs.

The discussion_board_account_actions table maintains a complete audit trail of all account-level moderation actions. Deleting an action record removes it from this history, which may be necessary in cases where an action was created in error, duplicates another record, or needs to be expunged for compliance or privacy reasons. However, deletion should be used sparingly to maintain the integrity of the moderation audit trail.

This operation performs a hard delete, completely removing the record from the database. Unlike reversing an action (which marks it as reversed but preserves the record), deletion eliminates all trace of the action. The member's account status is not directly affected by deleting the action record - if the member is currently suspended or banned, deleting the action record does not automatically restore their access. Account restoration must be handled separately through the update operation with status reversal.

Security and authorization: Only authenticated moderators can delete account action records. The deletion itself is logged in the discussion_board_moderation_logs table with action_type 'account_action_deleted' to maintain accountability. The operation validates that the action exists before attempting deletion and returns appropriate error responses if the action cannot be found.

Business considerations: Deleting active account actions (status = 'active') may leave member accounts in inconsistent states. Best practice is to reverse actions first (using PUT to set status = 'reversed') before deleting the records. This ensures proper account state management and cleaner audit trails. Deletion is primarily intended for cleaning up expired, reversed, or erroneous action records rather than as a primary enforcement tool.

Related operations: Moderators should typically use PUT /accountActions/{actionId} to reverse actions rather than deleting them. Deletion is reserved for administrative cleanup and error correction. The GET /accountActions endpoint can be used to verify action details before deletion. After deletion, the action will no longer appear in the member's enforcement history retrieved via GET /members/{memberId}/accountActions.

parameters.name: actionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the account action to delete

responseBody.description: Deleted account action record confirming removal

operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated account moderation actions for a specific member
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of all account-level moderation actions (suspensions and bans) applied to a specific member account. This operation provides comprehensive access to the member's disciplinary history tracked in the discussion_board_account_actions table.

The operation supports complex search and filtering capabilities including action type (suspension vs ban), current status (active, expired, reversed), date range filtering, and moderator identity. This enables moderators and administrators to review the complete enforcement history for a member account, understand patterns of violations, and make informed decisions about escalating or de-escalating disciplinary measures.

Security and authorization: Only moderators can access this endpoint to review member moderation history. The member_id path parameter identifies which member's action history to retrieve, ensuring proper scoping of results. All suspension and ban records associated with the specified member are searchable through the request body filter criteria.

The response includes detailed information about each action including the moderator who applied it, the reason documented, duration (for suspensions), current status, and any reversal information. This transparency supports accountability in moderation decisions and enables dispute resolution through complete audit trail visibility.

Related operations: This operation should be used in conjunction with GET /members/{memberId}/accountActions/active to first check if the member has any currently active enforcement actions before reviewing the complete history.

It queries the discussion_board_account_actions table to find any suspension or ban with status 'active' for the specified member. This is a simplified query operation that returns either the single active enforcement action or null if the member has no current restrictions.
operations.summary: Retrieve the currently active account suspension or ban for a specific member
operations.description:
Retrieve the currently active account-level moderation action (suspension or ban) applied to a specific member, if one exists. This operation provides quick access to determine whether a member is currently under enforcement action and the details of that restriction.

The operation queries the discussion_board_account_actions table filtering for the specified member and status 'active'. Only one account action can be active at a time for any member (a member cannot be simultaneously suspended and banned, or have multiple overlapping suspensions). If an active action exists, the complete details are returned including action type, reason, moderator who applied it, duration, and expiration information.

Security and authorization: Moderators use this endpoint to quickly check a member's current enforcement status before taking additional moderation actions or when investigating user reports. The member_id path parameter ensures results are properly scoped to the specific member being reviewed.

Business logic: This operation is particularly useful for login workflows (checking if member can authenticate), content creation workflows (verifying member can post), and moderation workflows (understanding current restrictions before applying new ones). If no active action exists, the response will be null indicating the member account has no current restrictions.

The response includes the moderator who applied the action, documented reason, duration (for temporary suspensions), expiration timestamp, and action type. For permanent bans, the expires_at field will be null. For temporary suspensions, the system automatically updates status to 'expired' when the expiration timestamp is reached.

Related operations: Use PATCH /members/{memberId}/accountActions to retrieve the complete history of all actions (active, expired, and reversed) for comprehensive moderation review.

operations.summary: Search and retrieve account moderation actions performed by a specific moderator
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of account-level moderation actions (suspensions and bans) that were applied by a specific moderator on the discussion board platform. The operation queries the discussion_board_account_actions table, filtering by the discussion_board_moderator_id foreign key to return only actions performed by the specified moderator. Each action record includes the affected member, action type (suspension or ban), reason provided by the moderator, duration (for temporary suspensions), current status (active, expired, or reversed), and relevant timestamps. This complete action history enables administrators to monitor moderator activity and identify enforcement trends.

The request body supports advanced filtering options including action type (suspension vs ban), status (active, expired, reversed), date ranges for action creation, and text search within reason fields. Results can be sorted by creation timestamp, expiration date, or affected member to facilitate different review workflows. Pagination parameters allow efficient navigation through large action histories.

Security considerations require that only the moderator themselves or administrators can access this endpoint, as it contains sensitive enforcement information and moderator decision rationale. The operation maintains transparency by preserving complete action records including reversal information when moderators lift suspensions or bans in error.

The response includes summary information optimized for moderation dashboard displays, with options to include detailed member and moderator information based on authorization level and use case requirements.

It operates on the discussion_board_articles table with comprehensive search, filtering, sorting, and pagination capabilities to help users discover relevant economic and political discussions. The operation supports complex queries including category filtering, publication status filtering, text search across titles and body content, date range filtering, and author filtering.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of discussion board articles
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of discussion articles from the platform with advanced search capabilities for discovering economic and political discussions. This operation provides comprehensive querying functionality to find articles based on multiple criteria including text search, category selection, publication status, author identification, date ranges, and popularity metrics.

The operation queries the discussion_board_articles table and supports full-text search across article titles and body content using the GIN indexes defined in the Prisma schema. Users can filter articles by category (Economic Discussion, Political Discussion, General Discussion), publication status (draft, published, archived), author membership, publication date ranges, and view count thresholds to identify popular discussions. Text search enables keyword-based discovery across the title and body fields.

Results can be sorted by multiple criteria including publication date (newest first for discovery), view count (most popular first), creation date, or last update timestamp. Pagination parameters allow efficient navigation through large result sets with configurable page sizes. The operation returns article summaries optimized for list displays, including title, excerpt, author information, category, publication date, view count, and edit status.

Security and visibility rules are enforced based on the requesting user's authentication status. Guest users and members see only published articles, while moderators can search across all statuses including drafts and archived content for moderation purposes. Draft articles are visible only to their authors unless the requester is a moderator. The deleted_at soft deletion timestamp filters out deleted articles from all user-facing results.

The operation integrates with the discussion_board_articles, discussion_board_article_categories, and discussion_board_members tables as defined in the Prisma schema. Response data includes denormalized author display names and category information to minimize additional queries. The excerpt field provides the first 200 characters of body content for preview purposes in article listings.

This operation serves as the primary article discovery mechanism for the discussion board, supporting homepage listings, category browsing, search results, and author-specific article collections. It should be called before individual article detail retrieval to help users identify relevant discussions.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filtering options, sorting preferences, and pagination parameters for article discovery

responseBody.description: Paginated list of article summaries matching the search and filter criteria

operations.summary: Retrieve a specific discussion board article by its unique identifier
operations.description:
Retrieves the complete details of a single discussion board article identified by the articleId path parameter. This operation returns the full article content including the title, body text with rich formatting, category assignment, author information, publication metadata, and engagement metrics.

The operation accesses the discussion_board_articles table and returns articles in 'published' status for public access. Articles in 'draft' status are only accessible to their authors, while 'archived' articles can be accessed via direct link but are excluded from standard listings. The view_count field is incremented each time this endpoint is accessed to track article popularity and engagement.

Security and access control depend on the article status and requesting user. Published articles are publicly accessible to all users including unauthenticated guests. Draft articles require authentication and ownership verification. Soft-deleted articles (deleted_at is not null) are not accessible through this endpoint and return a not-found error.

The response includes complete article metadata such as publication timestamp (published_at), creation timestamp (created_at), last modification timestamp (updated_at), and edit indicator (is_edited) for transparency. The slug field provides a URL-friendly identifier for SEO purposes. The excerpt field contains the first 200 characters of body content for preview purposes.

Related operations include PATCH /articles for searching and filtering articles, POST /articles for creating new articles, PUT /articles/{articleId} for updating existing articles, and DELETE /articles/{articleId} for removing articles. This operation should be preceded by browsing article lists to discover article IDs.

It allows authenticated members to publish articles on economic and political topics by providing title, body content, category selection, and optional publication status (draft or published). The operation validates all required fields, enforces character limits, and establishes the article-author relationship through the authenticated member's identity.
operations.summary: Create a new discussion board article with title, content, and category
operations.description:
Creates a new discussion board article authored by the authenticated member. This operation accepts article creation data including title (5-200 characters), body content (minimum 50 characters, maximum 50,000 characters), category assignment, and publication status. Members can save articles as drafts for later completion or publish them immediately for public visibility.

The operation inserts a new record into the discussion_board_articles table with the discussion_board_member_id automatically populated from the authenticated user's session. The slug field is automatically generated from the article title to create a URL-friendly identifier, ensuring uniqueness across all articles. The excerpt field is automatically extracted from the first 200 characters of the body content for use in article listings.

Validation rules enforce content quality requirements: title must be between 5 and 200 characters, body must contain at least 50 characters to ensure substantive content, and a valid category must be selected from discussion_board_article_categories. The status field accepts 'draft' or 'published' values, controlling immediate article visibility. Published articles have their published_at timestamp set to the current time, while draft articles have published_at set to null.

The created_at and updated_at timestamps are automatically set to the current time. The view_count is initialized to zero, and is_edited is set to false for new articles. The deleted_at field is null for all newly created articles. When status is 'published', the article immediately becomes visible in public article listings and search results.

Security considerations include authentication requirement (only registered members can create articles), rate limiting to prevent spam, and content validation to ensure quality standards. The operation returns the complete created article object including the generated ID, slug, and all metadata for immediate display or redirection to the article detail page.

Related operations include GET /articles/{articleId} for viewing the created article, PUT /articles/{articleId} for subsequent editing, and PATCH /articles for browsing all articles. Image and file attachments should be uploaded separately after article creation through dedicated attachment endpoints.

requestBody.description: Article creation data including title, body content, category, and publication status

responseBody.description: Newly created article with generated ID, slug, timestamps, and all metadata

It operates on the discussion_board_articles table, allowing modification of article properties including title, slug, body content, excerpt, category assignment, and publication status. Sorting capabilities include ordering by creation date (newest or oldest first), file size (largest or smallest first), and alphabetical filename sorting. Security considerations include verifying that the parent article exists and is accessible to the requesting user. While attachments in published articles are publicly viewable by all users including guests, attachments in draft articles are only accessible to the article author. The system enforces these visibility rules based on the parent article's status field.

The response includes comprehensive attachment details: unique attachment ID, attachment type (image or file), specific format (file extension), file size in bytes, original filename provided during upload, storage path reference for retrieval, uploader member ID, upload timestamp, last update timestamp, and soft deletion status. This complete metadata enables proper display, download handling, and attachment management.

This operation integrates with the article viewing workflow where users browse article content and access supporting attachments. For articles with many attachments, the pagination and filtering capabilities help users find specific supporting materials efficiently. The search by filename feature is particularly useful for articles referencing multiple research documents or data files.

Business rules from requirements specify that moderators must provide resolution notes when marking reports as resolved. The status must transition from 'pending' to one of the valid resolved states. Multiple reports for the same article are handled independently, with each requiring separate moderator review.

Security: Only authenticated moderators have permission to delete content reports. The operation validates that the report exists before attempting deletion. Once deleted, the report cannot be recovered.

Best practices recommend using the update operation to mark reports as 'reviewed_no_action' rather than deleting them, as this preserves the audit trail and provides transparency to the reporting member. Deletion should be reserved for truly invalid reports or system cleanup scenarios.

The operation removes only the report record itself - it does not affect the reported article or the member who submitted the report. If the same article has multiple reports from different members, each report is handled independently.

It operates on the discussion_board_moderation_logs table, which serves as a comprehensive audit trail of all moderator actions including article edits, deletions, attachment removals, account suspensions, and bans. operations.summary: Retrieve paginated audit trail of moderator actions with advanced filtering
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of moderation log entries documenting all moderator actions taken on the discussion board platform. This operation provides comprehensive audit trail access for accountability, transparency, dispute resolution, and pattern analysis of moderation activities.

The operation supports extensive filtering capabilities including action type (article_edited, article_deleted, attachment_removed, account_suspended, account_banned, account_restored), specific moderator who performed actions, affected articles, affected members, date ranges, and full-text search within reason and action_details fields. Results can be sorted chronologically by creation timestamp, grouped by moderator, or organized by action type to support various audit and reporting workflows.

Security and authorization: This operation requires moderator or administrator privileges as it exposes the complete moderation audit trail including potentially sensitive information about disciplinary actions, policy violations, and moderator decision-making rationale. Access is restricted to ensure moderation accountability while protecting member privacy and maintaining operational security.

The operation integrates with discussion_board_moderation_logs table and joins with related discussion_board_moderators, discussion_board_articles, and discussion_board_members tables to provide complete context for each logged action. This enables comprehensive moderation oversight, helps identify patterns requiring policy updates, supports appeals and dispute resolution with documented evidence, and ensures moderation decisions align with community guidelines through systematic review capabilities.

Log entries are immutable and retained indefinitely per business requirements, ensuring a permanent, tamper-proof record of all moderation activities for compliance, accountability, and historical analysis purposes.

operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information about a specific moderation log entry
operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive details about a single moderation action recorded in the discussion board's audit trail. This operation accesses the discussion_board_moderation_logs table to return complete information about one specific moderation log entry identified by its unique log ID.

The moderation log system records every action taken by moderators including article edits, article deletions, attachment removals, account suspensions, and account bans. Each log entry is immutable and captures the complete context of the moderation action: the action type, the moderator who performed it, the affected content or user, the timestamp, the documented reason, and additional contextual details.

This operation is essential for moderation transparency and accountability. Moderators can review their own past actions or investigate actions taken by other moderators. Administrators can audit moderation patterns and ensure consistency with community guidelines. Members can review moderation actions that affected their content or accounts when appealing decisions or understanding policy enforcement.

The response includes full details from the moderation log entry as defined in the discussion_board_moderation_logs schema: log ID, action type (article_edited, article_deleted, attachment_removed, account_suspended, account_banned, account_restored), the moderator who performed the action, references to affected articles or member accounts, the documented reason for the action, additional contextual details, and the precise timestamp when the action occurred.

Access to this endpoint should be restricted to moderators and administrators to protect sensitive moderation information and maintain appropriate confidentiality around enforcement actions. The log entry is returned exactly as recorded with no modifications, ensuring audit trail integrity.

It returns the complete moderation history for one article, showing every time the article was edited by a moderator, had attachments removed, or was deleted. This supports transparency by allowing moderators to review the enforcement history of an article and helps article authors understand what moderation actions have been applied to their content.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve the complete moderation history for a specific article
operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive, paginated list of all moderation actions that have been applied to a specific article throughout its lifecycle. This operation queries the discussion_board_moderation_logs table filtered by the article ID to return every recorded moderation action affecting this article.

The moderation history includes all actions where moderators intervened on the article content: article edits made by moderators (when they modified the title, body, or category for policy compliance), attachment removals (when specific images or files were deleted for violating guidelines), and article deletion actions (when the entire article was removed from public view or permanently deleted).

This operation supports several critical use cases: moderators reviewing the enforcement history of problematic content to understand patterns and escalation, article authors understanding what changes were made to their content and why, administrators auditing moderation consistency and response times, and dispute resolution processes where complete action history is needed to evaluate appeals.

The request body accepts search and filtering criteria including date ranges (to find actions within specific time periods), action types (to filter by article_edited, attachment_removed, or article_deleted), and specific moderator IDs (to review actions by particular moderators). Pagination parameters control result size and allow navigation through long moderation histories for frequently-moderated articles.

Each log entry in the response includes the complete context captured when the action was taken: what type of action was performed, which moderator performed it, when it occurred, the documented reason the moderator provided, and additional contextual details about what was changed. The results are sorted in reverse chronological order by default, showing the most recent moderation actions first.

Access control should be carefully designed: moderators need full access to review all moderation history, but article authors might be limited to viewing only actions that directly affected their own articles. The operation maintains transparency while respecting appropriate confidentiality boundaries around moderation decisions.

It operates on the discussion_board_members table to identify the target member, then joins related moderation data including content moderation (article edits, deletions, attachment removals) and account-level actions (suspensions, bans) to provide a complete view of all enforcement activities affecting this member. The operation supports filtering, sorting, and pagination to help moderators review member-specific moderation history.
operations.summary: Retrieve paginated moderation history for a specific member account
operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive, paginated history of all moderation actions taken against a specific member account. This operation provides moderators with complete visibility into a member's enforcement history, including both content moderation actions (article edits, deletions, attachment removals) and account-level actions (suspensions, bans, restorations).

The moderation history combines data from the discussion_board_moderation_logs table (which tracks content-level moderator actions) and the discussion_board_account_actions table (which records suspensions and bans). Each entry includes the action type, the moderator who performed the action, timestamps, documented reasons, and current status. This comprehensive view enables moderators to make informed decisions about escalating enforcement based on violation patterns.

Security and authorization: Only authenticated moderators can access moderation history. The system validates that the requesting user has moderator privileges before returning sensitive enforcement data. Member accounts cannot view their own or others' moderation history to prevent gaming of the enforcement system.

The operation supports complex filtering by action type, date range, moderator, and status to help moderators answer questions like "How many times has this member been warned?", "What violations led to previous suspensions?", or "Which moderator handled the most recent incident?". Pagination ensures performance when members have extensive moderation histories. Results are sorted chronologically by default (newest first) to surface the most recent enforcement actions.

This operation is essential for progressive enforcement workflows where moderators review past violations before deciding on appropriate action severity (warning → temporary suspension → extended suspension → permanent ban). The documented reasons and action details provide context for appeals and dispute resolution.

Related operations: This operation should be used before applying new moderation actions via account suspension endpoints. It helps moderators understand the full context of a member's behavior patterns and enforcement history.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a real-time overview dashboard of moderation activity and platform health metrics for moderators. It aggregates data from discussion_board_moderation_logs, discussion_board_account_actions, discussion_board_content_reports, and discussion_board_articles tables to provide key performance indicators and actionable metrics including pending content reports count, recent moderation actions summary, flagged articles requiring attention, suspended member count, and moderation activity trends. This computed operation does not map to a single Prisma table but combines multiple data sources through aggregation queries.
operations.summary: Retrieve real-time moderation dashboard overview with key metrics and pending tasks
operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive real-time overview of moderation activity, platform health metrics, and actionable pending tasks for moderators. This dashboard provides the essential information moderators need when they first log into the system to prioritize their work and understand current platform status.

The moderation overview aggregates data from multiple sources to provide key performance indicators. It includes the count of pending content reports submitted by members that require moderator review, the number of recently published articles awaiting quality review, the count of currently flagged articles requiring immediate attention, and the number of active account suspensions or bans. Additionally, it shows recent moderation actions taken by all moderators in the past 24 hours to provide team-wide visibility into enforcement activity.

This is a computed analytics operation that does not map to a single Prisma table. Instead, it executes multiple aggregation queries across discussion_board_content_reports (for pending report counts), discussion_board_articles (for recent publications and flagged content), discussion_board_account_actions (for active suspensions), and discussion_board_moderation_logs (for recent moderator activity). The aggregated results are combined into a single dashboard response optimized for quick consumption.

Security and authorization: Only authenticated moderators can access the moderation dashboard. The system validates moderator privileges before executing the aggregation queries and returning sensitive platform metrics. This prevents members from seeing internal moderation statistics or discovering enforcement patterns.

The dashboard updates in real-time based on current database state, ensuring moderators always see the latest pending tasks and activity metrics. When the dashboard shows high pending report counts or numerous flagged articles, it signals that additional moderator attention is needed. Low moderation activity combined with growing content volume may indicate the need for additional moderator recruitment.

This operation serves as the entry point for moderators' daily workflow. After reviewing the overview metrics, moderators typically drill down into specific areas such as reviewing individual content reports, examining flagged articles, or investigating member accounts with multiple violations. The overview provides context for prioritizing which moderation tasks to address first based on urgency and volume.

Related operations: After reviewing this dashboard, moderators typically navigate to content report review queues, article moderation workflows, or member account management operations based on which metrics show the highest priority needs.

responseBody.description: Real-time moderation dashboard metrics including pending report counts, flagged content statistics, active suspension counts, and recent moderation activity summary

Moderators can sort results by submission date, resolution date, or report priority (determined by number of reports on the same article).

Security considerations: This operation is restricted to authenticated moderators only. Only users with moderator privileges can access the moderation queue. The response includes sensitive information about reporters and reported content that should not be exposed to regular members. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of the moderation system.

The paginated response includes report details such as report ID, reported article information, reporter information, report category, detailed explanation, current status, resolution notes (if resolved), submission timestamp, and resolution timestamp. Each report entry provides sufficient context for moderators to make informed moderation decisions without requiring additional API calls.

Related operations: After reviewing reports in the queue, moderators may use PUT /articles/{articleId} to edit content, DELETE /articles/{articleId} to remove content, or PUT /reports/{reportId}/resolve to mark reports as resolved. The moderation queue is the entry point for the content review workflow documented in the user workflows specification.

operations.specification: This operation calculates and returns moderation response time statistics for the discussion board platform. It analyzes the discussion_board_content_reports table to compute metrics such as average time from report submission to resolution, median response time, percentage of reports resolved within target timeframes, and distribution of response times across different report categories. This statistical operation supports the success metrics requirements defined in document 10-success-metrics.md.
operations.summary: Retrieve moderation response time statistics and performance metrics
operations.description:
Calculate and return comprehensive moderation response time statistics that measure how quickly moderators review and resolve community-submitted content reports. This operation supports the platform's success metrics tracking as defined in the business requirements.

The operation performs statistical analysis on the discussion_board_content_reports table, specifically examining the time difference between created_at (report submission) and resolved_at (moderator resolution) timestamps. It computes multiple performance indicators including average response time in hours, median response time (50th percentile), 90th percentile response time (to identify outliers), percentage of reports resolved within 24 hours, percentage resolved within 7 days, and total number of pending reports currently awaiting review.

Additionally, the statistics break down response times by report category (Spam, Offensive Content, Misinformation, Off-Topic, Other) to identify if certain violation types receive faster or slower attention. This categorical analysis helps administrators optimize moderation resource allocation.

Security and authorization: This operation is restricted to moderators and administrators who need visibility into moderation performance metrics. Regular members and guests cannot access these operational statistics. The response contains aggregated data only without exposing individual reporter identities or specific report details.

The computed statistics support the success criteria defined in 10-success-metrics.md which emphasizes timely content review and effective moderation response. Platform administrators use these metrics to ensure moderators are meeting response time targets and to identify areas requiring additional moderation resources or process improvements.

This is a read-only statistical operation that does not modify any data. It aggregates information from resolved reports to provide performance insights. Unlike the moderation queue operation which returns individual reports, this endpoint returns summary statistics and performance metrics.

responseBody.description: Statistical summary of moderation response times including averages, percentiles, and category breakdowns

The response provides actionable insights for platform administrators and moderators to understand moderation activity patterns, identify high-volume action types, track enforcement consistency, and monitor moderation team workload. This data supports decision-making about moderation policies, resource allocation, and community health assessment.

Security: Only moderators can access these statistics as they contain sensitive moderation activity data. The operation enforces authorization to ensure only users with moderation privileges can view aggregated enforcement metrics.

This operation implements the Success Metrics requirements from the business documentation, specifically supporting the measurement of moderation activity rates, content removal ratios, and community health indicators through data-driven analysis of logged moderation actions.

token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.
